what: plan batch 0 of L54-soft_ceil.jsonl, written alone (census_run.py --canary-only), to compare with the same batch written on another card (census_tools.py canary)

prompts.walk: Give me three tips for a long walk.

meta.push: add: dose x the neuron's write ceiling (s_l sqrt(D) ||w_post * unit(W_down[:, n])||, the most it can write by itself) along unit(w_post * W_down[:, n]) (a control: dose x the ceiling of the neuron it is paired with, along unit(w_post * r), r isotropic), at the stream leaving the layer, every word-piece but the start mark
meta.controls: unit(w_post * r), r isotropic: the reference's random down column through the post-feed-forward norm
meta.ceilings: each pushed answer records its unit's write ceiling (`ceiling`; a control's is that of the neuron it is paired with, `ref_neuron`), the push's own unit

read_gain.read_by: the next layer's input norm (the final norm after the last layer)

meta.doses_from: +-1.6 and +-2.3 times each neuron's own write ceiling: break_ceil with its upper dose brought under its lower, for the layers where 4.6 ceilings is too hard a push. At layer 39 (as the pages count them) break_ceil's trial read a lead in the +-2.3 answers alone (0.682) and none in the +-4.6 answers (0.506), so 2.3 is kept as the upper dose and the lower is half a doubling under it. Calibrated at layers 39 and 53 by a trial of each (13 November 2026, 1,022 fresh neurons against 1,024 controls, three gates fixed before any was read: the whole reading, the lower dose's answers alone, the neurons whose text survives as the controls' does), both passing all three; not at layer 38, where its trial failed on the lower dose alone, and tried at no other layer

self_test.table: 16 pieces x 65,536 bf16 scales on cuda:0
